title: Start making something
coreMove: An idea is worth little until it becomes a thing people can use, buy, or reject; making converts imagination into evidence, and execution, not the notion, decides the outcome.

exampleSpecs.audience: founders who keep refining a concept instead of building
exampleSpecs.stakes: build the smallest working version or keep polishing the pitch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist chooses to make a real artifact over guarding the idea

exampleSpecs.audience: inventors hoping to sell a concept before building
exampleSpecs.stakes: sell the unbuilt idea or build proof first
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist learns an unexecuted idea fetches almost nothing

exampleSpecs.audience: teams running endless interviews before building
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep interviewing or ship a small thing people can react to
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist weighs talk-based feedback against reactions to a real artifact

exampleSpecs.audience: makers waiting for a perfect plan before starting
exampleSpecs.stakes: wait for every answer or start and let building force the choices
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: beginning forces tradeoffs that planning had postponed

exampleSpecs.audience: founders who think the idea itself is the advantage
exampleSpecs.stakes: treat the shared idea as decisive or treat execution as decisive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two teams with the same idea diverge on execution quality

exampleSpecs.stakes: ship anything fast and sloppy or make one real, testable thing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist separates frantic motion from making a real artifact
